newsitem.title: GERMANY: MG Handel sees profits higher in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: MG Handel sees profits higher in 1996/97.

text.p: MG Handel AG, the trading subsidiary of Metallgesellschaft AG, said on Wednesday that it expected its profit to improve in the current business year after pretax profits fell in the year ended September 30.
The company's chairman, Horst Siedentopf, told a news conference that developments in the first few months of the current business year pointed to improved profits.
For 1995/96, the company reported pretax profit of 33 million marks, down from 55 million in 1994/95.

Siedentopf said the reasons behind the slide in profits lay in a further loss at its subsidiary MG Erz- & Metallhandel GmbH in Frankfurt, which includes Metal Concentrates International Inc in New York.

The unit posted a pre-tax loss of 33.8 million marks after 30.1 million a year earlier. MG Handel said MCII had posted an operating profit but had had to make 18 million marks of provisions for writedowns on holdings.

The company's other units were in profit, Siedentopf said, although profits in some areas were sharply lower. MG Ltd, which trades in non-ferrous metals, had seen its profit more than halved to 35 million marks by the fall in copper prices.

MG Handel's turnover rose to 7.1 billion marks in 1995/96 compared with 8.9 billion marks in 1996/97. Siedentopf said that the fall was partly due to the sale of Dutch group Jewometaal, which had turnover of 679 million marks.
MG Handel employed 495 people at end-September, 236 less than a year earlier. Of the job losses, 202 were due to the sale of Jewometaal.
